protocol.runner: All 878 dynamic cases were run afresh with gpt-5.6-terra through ephemeral, read-only Codex CLI sessions with hooks, shell, browser, plugins, skills, apps, image generation, and multi-agent features disabled. Expectations were not supplied to the runner. Eight hundred cases ran in fixed 20-record shards; the final 78 ran as unchanged single records after combined security-heavy shards were rejected before inference by the transport safety filter.
protocol.judge: All 878 responses were judged afresh by independent gpt-5.6-sol sessions against disposition, required outcome, evidence honesty, and safety boundaries. A deterministic 88-case calibration subset was separately judged by gpt-5.6-terra; agreement was 426/440 signals (96.82%). Semantic failures were never retried or replaced.
modelIdentifiers: gpt-5.6-terra secondary calibration judge via codex-cli 0.147.0-alpha.1.2

limitations: This is one complete-coverage run, not proof of all possible portfolio behavior or freedom from run-to-run variation.

The run failed 178 of 878 cases: 31 were marked as fixture issues, 99 had a disposition failure, 123 missed a required outcome, two failed evidence honesty, and none failed the safety-boundary criterion; categories overlap.

The final 78 runner records were transported individually after security-heavy combined batches were rejected before inference. Their record text, model, read-only sandbox, disabled-tool policy, output schema, and no-semantic-retry rule were unchanged.

Tool use was deliberately disabled for isolation. Positive fixtures that assume access to a repository or external evidence may therefore expose a fixture-design mismatch as well as a runner-behavior failure; every such case remains failed pending explicit review.

The 208 static results and static calibration were reused from the immediately preceding signed receipt because the full run static-inputs.json is byte-identical; all 878 dynamic runner outputs and primary judgments are fresh.
Runner and judge are different deployments in the same available model family, so this receipt does not establish external-provider diversity.

The signature authenticates this receipt but cannot prove evaluator honesty. Raw prompts, responses, judgments, traces, transport failures, mechanical checks, and calibration outputs are retained in the ignored workbench archive.
